newsitem.title: USA: DC board rejects FY 98 city budget for third time.
newsitem.headline: DC board rejects FY 98 city budget for third time.

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board on Tuesday rejected for the third time in three months a proposed fiscal 1998 budget for the financially struggling city, a D.C. official said.

The five-member panel headed by economist Andrew Brimmer concluded that the $5.2 billion budget approved by the council in late April inadequately funds D.C.'s troubled public school system, corrections and other programs.
The budget now goes back to the council, which has two weeks to act, for a rewrite. The control board has until June 15 to send a final proposed budget for D.C. to Capitol Hill committees for review.
The control board on March 3 and later on April 2 rejected fiscal 1998 budgets proposed by Mayor Marion Barry, saying they shortchanged schools and public safety.
The panel then forwarded the matter to the D.C. council.
A spokesman for the control board was unavailable for comments.
